grammar.title: Change in ability: ようになる
grammar.explanation:
Potential or nonvolitional verb + ようになる describes a change that makes an ability or situation possible. Negative verbs can describe ceasing to do something.

Formation: Potential or other nonvolitional verb + ようになる; negative verb + ようになる can describe a newly absent habit.

Usage and cautions: This foregrounds change over time, not a single decision or an effort. To describe gaining ability, use a potential verb before ようになる. Compare ようにする, which expresses deliberate effort. Polite past ようになりました reports that the change has occurred.

examples.ja: 日本語の新聞が読めるようになりました。
examples.en: I have become able to read Japanese newspapers.

examples.ja: 練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。
examples.reading: れんしゅうして、じてんしゃにのれるようになりました。
examples.en: After practicing, I became able to ride a bicycle.

examples.ja: 最近、甘い物を食べないようになりました。
examples.reading: さいきん、あまいものをたべないようになりました。
examples.en: Recently I have stopped eating sweet things.

questions.prompt: Choose a change in ability.
choices: 泳がなければならない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “泳げるようになった”. Potential 泳げる plus ようになった describes becoming able to swim.

questions.prompt: Describe newly gained reading ability: 漢字が読める＿。
questions.explanation: Potential 読める plus ようになった describes a change into being able to read, not a decision.

questions.prompt: Choose a change in a nonvolitional situation.
choices: この町にもバスが来たがっている。
この町にもバスが来てみた。
この町にもバスが来るようになった。
この町にもバスが来ることにした。
questions.explanation: 来るようになった means buses now serve the town; it does not attribute personal decision or desire to a bus.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。
choices: I must practice riding a bicycle tomorrow.
After practicing, I became able to ride a bicycle.
I decided not to ride a bicycle.
I used to ride a bicycle but cannot now.
questions.explanation: “練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。” means “After practicing, I became able to ride a bicycle.” in this example. This foregrounds change over time, not a single decision or an effort.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 最近、甘い物を食べないようになりました。
choices: Recently I have stopped eating sweet things.
Recently I have started eating more sweets.
I am forbidden to eat sweets from tomorrow.
I have never eaten anything sweet.
questions.explanation: “最近、甘い物を食べないようになりました。” means “Recently I have stopped eating sweet things.” in this example. This foregrounds change over time, not a single decision or an effort.

grammar.title: Maintaining habits: ようにする
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary form or ない-form + ようにする expresses a conscious effort to establish or maintain a habit, rather than a single firm decision.

Formation: Dictionary or negative verb + ようにする; ようにしている emphasizes an ongoing conscious practice.

Usage and cautions: The speaker tries to make an action habitual or avoids a recurring problem. This does not guarantee success on every occasion. Contrast ようになる for a change that has developed and ことにする for making a decision. Use a negative verb for an avoidance habit.

examples.ja: 毎日、野菜を食べるようにしています。
examples.en: I make a point of eating vegetables every day.

examples.ja: 寝る前にスマホを見ないようにしています。
examples.reading: ねるまえにスマホをみないようにしています。
examples.en: I make a point of not looking at my phone before bed.

examples.ja: 毎朝、少し歩くようにしています。
examples.reading: まいあさ、すこしあるくようにしています。
examples.en: I make an effort to walk a little every morning.

questions.prompt: Choose 'try to avoid being late'.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “遅れないようにする”. ようにする with ない expresses a deliberate effort not to do something.

questions.prompt: Complete an avoidance habit: 忘れ物をしない＿しています。
questions.explanation: しないようにしている expresses an ongoing effort to avoid leaving things behind.

questions.prompt: Which describes deliberate habit rather than acquired ability?
choices: 野菜を食べているところだ。
野菜を食べるようにしている。
野菜を食べられるようになった。
野菜を食べたことがある。
questions.explanation: ようにしている marks conscious practice; ようになった marks a developed change, and the others experience or phase.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 寝る前にスマホを見ないようにしています。
choices: I make a point of not looking at my phone before bed.
I have become unable to see my phone.
I must look at my phone before sleeping.
I looked at my phone only last night.
questions.explanation: “寝る前にスマホを見ないようにしています。” means “I make a point of not looking at my phone before bed.” in this example. The speaker tries to make an action habitual or avoids a recurring problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 毎朝、少し歩くようにしています。
choices: I became unable to walk in the morning.
I walked only once this morning.
I intend to stop all morning walks.
I make an effort to walk a little every morning.
questions.explanation: “毎朝、少し歩くようにしています。” means “I make an effort to walk a little every morning.” in this example. The speaker tries to make an action habitual or avoids a recurring problem.

grammar.title: Personal decisions: ことにする
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary or negative form + ことにする means deciding to do or not do something. ことにしている can describe a self-imposed rule.

Formation: Dictionary / negative verb + ことにする; ことにした reports a decision, and ことにしている a personal rule.

Usage and cautions: The construction emphasizes the decision-maker’s agency. It does not merely describe an externally imposed schedule. The negative belongs inside the clause for a decision not to act. A polite ending does not make the embedded verb polite: 行くことにしました.

examples.ja: 今年は車を買わないことにしました。
examples.en: I decided not to buy a car this year.

examples.ja: 健康のため、階段を使うことにしました。
examples.reading: けんこうのため、かいだんをつかうことにしました。
examples.en: I decided to use the stairs for my health.

examples.ja: 日曜日は仕事をしないことにしています。
examples.reading: にちようびはしごとをしないことにしています。
examples.en: I make it a personal rule not to work on Sundays.

questions.prompt: Which is a personal decision?
choices: 留学することになった
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “留学することにした”. ことにする foregrounds the decision-maker's agency; ことになる presents an arrangement.

questions.prompt: Express a personal decision not to buy: 車を買わない＿。
questions.explanation: 買わないことにした foregrounds the decision not to buy; the other expressions describe change or timing.

questions.prompt: Complete a personal rule: 毎晩、日記を書くことに＿。
questions.explanation: ことにしている describes a self-imposed practice; the decision is maintained as a rule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 健康のため、階段を使うことにしました。
choices: It was decided by others that I cannot use the stairs.
I have never used the stairs.
I happened to find some stairs.
I decided to use the stairs for my health.
questions.explanation: “健康のため、階段を使うことにしました。” means “I decided to use the stairs for my health.” in this example. The construction emphasizes the decision-maker’s agency.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 日曜日は仕事をしないことにしています。
choices: I worked last Sunday by accident.
I am required by law to work on Sundays.
I make it a personal rule not to work on Sundays.
I have become unable to work on Sundays.
questions.explanation: “日曜日は仕事をしないことにしています。” means “I make it a personal rule not to work on Sundays.” in this example. The construction emphasizes the decision-maker’s agency.

grammar.title: Arrangements: ことになる
grammar.explanation:
ことになる presents an outcome, arrangement, or rule as decided by circumstances or others. It need not reveal exactly who decided it.

Formation: Dictionary / negative verb + ことになる; ことになっている describes an established rule or arrangement.

Usage and cautions: The result is presented as an arrangement or consequence without foregrounding who personally chose it. This can soften how a decision is announced. Contrast ことにする for an explicit personal decision. It does not imply that nobody participated in deciding.

examples.ja: 来月、大阪に転勤することになりました。
examples.en: It has been arranged that I will transfer to Osaka next month.

examples.ja: 来月から新しい部署で働くことになりました。
examples.reading: らいげつからあたらしいぶしょではたらくことになりました。
examples.en: It has been arranged that I will work in a new department from next month.

examples.ja: この建物では、靴を脱ぐことになっています。
examples.reading: このたてものでは、くつをぬぐことになっています。
examples.en: The rule in this building is to remove your shoes.

questions.prompt: Choose an externally presented arrangement.
choices: 会議は中止することになった
会議を中止することにした
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “会議は中止することになった”. ことになる presents the decision as a resulting arrangement.

questions.prompt: Announce an arranged cancellation: 試合は中止される＿。
questions.explanation: 中止されることになった presents the cancellation as the resulting arrangement, not the match’s own decision.

questions.prompt: Choose the expression for an established company rule.
choices: 会社では九時に出勤したばかりだ。
会社では九時に出勤してみたい。
会社では九時に出勤したことがない。
会社では九時に出勤することになっている。
questions.explanation: ことになっている describes the standing arrangement; the alternatives describe recency, desire and experience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 来月から新しい部署で働くことになりました。
choices: I refuse to work in a new department.
I can choose any department every day.
It has been arranged that I will work in a new department from next month.
I have worked in the new department for years.
questions.explanation: “来月から新しい部署で働くことになりました。” means “It has been arranged that I will work in a new department from next month.” in this example. The result is presented as an arrangement or consequence without foregrounding who personally chose it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この建物では、靴を脱ぐことになっています。
choices: I decided to buy shoes for this building.
The rule in this building is to remove your shoes.
I happen to be taking off my shoes right now.
Removing shoes is forbidden in this building.
questions.explanation: “この建物では、靴を脱ぐことになっています。” means “The rule in this building is to remove your shoes.” in this example. The result is presented as an arrangement or consequence without foregrounding who personally chose it.

grammar.title: Just completed: たばかり
grammar.explanation:
Past verb + ばかり means an event feels recent to the speaker. Unlike たところ, it can refer to a longer period if subjectively recent.

Formation: Plain past verb + ばかりだ / ばかりです. The verb remains past even when the overall sentence is nonpast.

Usage and cautions: Recency is judged by the speaker, not by an exact clock interval. A move last month may still feel recent. Compare たところ, which usually locates the immediate phase after completion. This use is distinct from noun + ばかり meaning only or nothing but.

examples.ja: 先月、日本に来たばかりです。
examples.en: I only came to Japan last month.

examples.ja: 昼ご飯を食べたばかりなので、おなかはすいていません。
examples.reading: ひるごはんをたべたばかりなので、おなかはすいていません。
examples.en: I have just eaten lunch, so I am not hungry.

examples.ja: 去年、この会社に入ったばかりです。
examples.reading: きょねん、このかいしゃにはいったばかりです。
examples.en: I only joined this company last year.

questions.prompt: Can たばかり refer to last month?
choices: Yes, but only with negative verbs
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “Yes, if it feels recent”. ばかり is subjective recency, not a fixed number of minutes.

questions.prompt: Complete subjective recency: 新しいパソコンを買っ＿ばかりです。
questions.explanation: 買ったばかり uses the plain past form to describe a purchase still felt to be recent.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation is NOT required by たばかり?
choices: The speaker considers the event recent.
The phrase contains a past-form verb.
The event happened within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: たばかり does not impose a seconds-long interval; subjective recency may extend much further.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 昼ご飯を食べたばかりなので、おなかはすいていません。
choices: I have just eaten lunch, so I am not hungry.
I am hungry because I have not eaten lunch.
I am about to start making lunch.
questions.explanation: “昼ご飯を食べたばかりなので、おなかはすいていません。” means “I have just eaten lunch, so I am not hungry.” in this example. Recency is judged by the speaker, not by an exact clock interval.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 去年、この会社に入ったばかりです。
choices: I only joined this company last year.
I will join this company next year.
I have never joined this company.
I left this company last year.
questions.explanation: “去年、この会社に入ったばかりです。” means “I only joined this company last year.” in this example. Recency is judged by the speaker, not by an exact clock interval.

grammar.title: Phases with ところ
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary form + ところ is just about to act; ているところ is in the middle; たところ is just finished. It locates the action's phase.

Formation: Dictionary verb + ところ: about to; ている + ところ: in progress; past verb + ところ: just finished.

Usage and cautions: ところ highlights a phase relative to the reference time. With でした the reference point can be in the past. It is not simply another tense ending. The physical-place meaning of ところ is separate, and たところ can have other narrative uses in longer sentences.

examples.ja: 今から出かけるところです。
examples.en: I am just about to go out.

examples.ja: 今、夕飯を作っているところです。
examples.reading: いま、ゆうはんをつくっているところです。
examples.en: I am in the middle of making dinner.

examples.ja: ちょうど駅に着いたところです。
examples.reading: ちょうどえきについたところです。
examples.en: I have just arrived at the station.

questions.prompt: Choose 'in the middle of eating'.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “食べているところ”. ているところ explicitly marks the ongoing phase.

questions.prompt: Say “I am just about to call”: 電話を＿ところです。
questions.explanation: Dictionary-form かけるところ describes the phase immediately before calling, unlike the past and progressive phases.

questions.prompt: What phase is 食べているところでした?
choices: Eating was in progress at that past time.
questions.explanation: ているところ marks an ongoing phase; でした places that phase at a past reference point.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 今、夕飯を作っているところです。
choices: I am in the middle of making dinner.
I am just about to eat dinner.
I have just finished making dinner.
questions.explanation: “今、夕飯を作っているところです。” means “I am in the middle of making dinner.” in this example. ところ highlights a phase relative to the reference time.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: ちょうど駅に着いたところです。
choices: I am about to leave for the station.
I am still traveling toward the station.
I used to live at the station.
I have just arrived at the station.
questions.explanation: “ちょうど駅に着いたところです。” means “I have just arrived at the station.” in this example. ところ highlights a phase relative to the reference time.

grammar.title: Expectation: はず
grammar.explanation:
Plain clause + はず expresses a reasoned expectation based on evidence or knowledge. It is not a desire, command, or absolute guarantee.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + はず; noun + のはず; な-adjective + なはず. Negative expectation: ないはず.

Usage and cautions: Use はず for a conclusion supported by a timetable, known facts or other evidence. It is not a request that someone ought to obey. はずだった can describe an expectation that later proved wrong. Do not equate reasonable expectation with absolute certainty.

examples.ja: 彼はもう着いているはずです。
examples.en: He should have arrived by now.

examples.ja: 今日は月曜日だから、銀行は開いているはずです。
examples.reading: きょうはげつようびだから、ぎんこうはあいているはずです。
examples.en: Since today is Monday, the bank should be open.

examples.ja: 彼女は医者のはずです。
examples.reading: かのじょはいしゃのはずです。
examples.en: She should be a doctor, as far as I know.

questions.prompt: Which expresses a reasoned expectation?
choices: 店は開いているはずだ
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “店は開いているはずだ”. はず marks an inference from what the speaker knows.

questions.prompt: Complete a noun expectation: 田中さんは学生＿はずです。
questions.explanation: A noun connects to はず with の: 学生のはずです.

questions.prompt: Choose an unfulfilled expectation.
choices: 荷物は昨日届くはずでしたが、まだ来ません。
荷物を昨日届けてください。
荷物は昨日届いたばかりです。
荷物を昨日届けたかったです。
questions.explanation: 届くはずでした reports the expected delivery, and まだ来ません explicitly shows the expectation was not met.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 今日は月曜日だから、銀行は開いているはずです。
choices: Please open the bank because it is Monday.
I want to work in a bank on Monday.
The bank is definitely closed every Monday.
Since today is Monday, the bank should be open.
questions.explanation: “今日は月曜日だから、銀行は開いているはずです。” means “Since today is Monday, the bank should be open.” in this example. Use はず for a conclusion supported by a timetable, known facts or other evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 彼女は医者のはずです。
choices: She wants to see a doctor.
She was forced to be a doctor.
She should be a doctor, as far as I know.
She ought to become a doctor someday.
questions.explanation: “彼女は医者のはずです。” means “She should be a doctor, as far as I know.” in this example. Use はず for a conclusion supported by a timetable, known facts or other evidence.

grammar.title: Partial denial: わけではない
grammar.explanation:
わけではない rejects an inference or generalization. It often means 'it is not that' or 'not necessarily', rather than a simple complete denial.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + わけではない; な-adjective / noun + なわけではない.

Usage and cautions: This rejects an inference, total claim or assumption, often without denying the whole underlying fact. いつも…わけではない means not always. というわけではない can quote a proposition before qualifying it. Distinguish partial denial from 全く…ない, a complete denial.

examples.ja: 甘い物が嫌いなわけではありません。
examples.en: It is not that I dislike sweet things.

examples.ja: 毎日外食するわけではありません。
examples.reading: まいにちがいしょくするわけではありません。
examples.en: It is not the case that I eat out every day.

examples.ja: 嫌いなわけではないですが、今日は食べたくありません。
examples.reading: きらいなわけではないですが、きょうはたべたくありません。
examples.en: It is not that I dislike it, but I do not want to eat it today.

questions.prompt: What does 全部知っているわけではない mean?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “I do not know everything”. The construction denies complete knowledge, not all knowledge.

questions.prompt: Deny “always easy”: いつも簡単＿わけではない。
questions.explanation: 簡単 is a な-adjective and connects to わけ with な; the statement rejects the claim that it is always easy.

questions.prompt: What does 全員が賛成したわけではない leave possible?
choices: Some people agreed, but not everyone.
questions.explanation: The denial targets 全員, the claim about all members; it does not require that no one agreed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 毎日外食するわけではありません。
choices: I always eat out every day.
I am prohibited from eating out.
It is not the case that I eat out every day.
I never eat out at all.
questions.explanation: “毎日外食するわけではありません。” means “It is not the case that I eat out every day.” in this example. This rejects an inference, total claim or assumption, often without denying the whole underlying fact.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 嫌いなわけではないですが、今日は食べたくありません。
choices: I did not eat it because it was forbidden.
It is not that I dislike it, but I do not want to eat it today.
I dislike it and never want to eat it.
I like it so much that I must eat it today.
questions.explanation: “嫌いなわけではないですが、今日は食べたくありません。” means “It is not that I dislike it, but I do not want to eat it today.” in this example. This rejects an inference, total claim or assumption, often without denying the whole underlying fact.

grammar.title: Difficulty doing: にくい・やすい
grammar.explanation:
Attach にくい or やすい to a verb stem to describe difficulty or ease in performing an action. These inflect as い-adjectives.

Formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい / にくい. These endings inflect like い-adjectives: やすかった, にくくない.

Usage and cautions: The pattern describes ease or difficulty of doing the verb, often as a property of a tool or situation. It does not mean cheap when attached as an auxiliary to a verb. Use the stem, not the dictionary form. Physical impossibility is stronger than simple にくい.

examples.ja: この説明は分かりにくいです。
examples.en: This explanation is difficult to understand.

examples.ja: このペンは書きやすいです。
examples.reading: このペンはかきやすいです。
examples.en: This pen is easy to write with.

examples.ja: この道は夜、歩きにくいです。
examples.reading: このみちはよる、あるきにくいです。
examples.en: This road is difficult to walk along at night.

questions.prompt: Choose 'easy to use'.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “使いやすい”. 使い is the verb stem and やすい describes ease.

questions.prompt: Choose “hard to read”.
questions.explanation: 読む has the stem 読み; adding にくい makes 読みにくい.

questions.prompt: Choose the past of 使いやすい.
questions.explanation: やすい inflects as an い-adjective: final い becomes かった in the past.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: このペンは書きやすいです。
choices: This pen was difficult to find.
This pen is easy to write with.
This pen is cheap to buy.
This pen cannot write at all.
questions.explanation: “このペンは書きやすいです。” means “This pen is easy to write with.” in this example. The pattern describes ease or difficulty of doing the verb, often as a property of a tool or situation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この道は夜、歩きにくいです。
choices: This road is difficult to walk along at night.
This road is easy to walk along at night.
This road becomes cheaper at night.
Walking here at night is strictly forbidden.
questions.explanation: “この道は夜、歩きにくいです。” means “This road is difficult to walk along at night.” in this example. The pattern describes ease or difficulty of doing the verb, often as a property of a tool or situation.

grammar.title: Unwanted tendency: がち
grammar.explanation:
Noun or verb stem + がち describes a tendency, usually something undesirable or frequent. It is not used for every neutral habit.

Formation: Verb ます-stem or selected noun + がち. Before a noun use がちな or がちの where idiomatic.

Usage and cautions: This marks a recurring, often undesirable tendency rather than a single event. Common combinations include 忘れがち, 遅れがち and 病気がち. It is not a general replacement for よく with every neutral habit. The tendency need not occur every single time.

examples.ja: 冬は運動不足になりがちです。
examples.en: In winter people tend to get too little exercise.

examples.ja: 忙しいと、朝ご飯を抜きがちです。
examples.reading: いそがしいと、あさごはんをぬきがちです。
examples.en: When busy, I tend to skip breakfast.

examples.ja: 祖父は最近、病気がちです。
examples.reading: そふはさいきん、びょうきがちです。
examples.en: My grandfather has been prone to illness recently.

questions.prompt: Choose a common undesirable tendency.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “忘れがち”. がち attaches to the stem 忘れ and marks a recurring tendency.

questions.prompt: Complete a recurring delay: 雨の日は電車が遅れ＿です。
questions.explanation: 遅れ is the stem of 遅れる; 遅れがち describes a tendency to be delayed on rainy days.

questions.prompt: Which context best fits 忘れがち?
choices: Frequently forgetting small tasks when busy
questions.explanation: がち describes a repeated tendency, here an unwanted tendency to forget; it is not permission or a one-time event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 忙しいと、朝ご飯を抜きがちです。
choices: When busy, I tend to skip breakfast.
When busy, I always eat a large breakfast.
I skipped breakfast only once in my life.
I am not allowed to eat breakfast.
questions.explanation: “忙しいと、朝ご飯を抜きがちです。” means “When busy, I tend to skip breakfast.” in this example. This marks a recurring, often undesirable tendency rather than a single event.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 祖父は最近、病気がちです。
choices: My grandfather recently became a doctor.
My grandfather has never been ill.
My grandfather has completely recovered forever.
My grandfather has been prone to illness recently.
questions.explanation: “祖父は最近、病気がちです。” means “My grandfather has been prone to illness recently.” in this example. This marks a recurring, often undesirable tendency rather than a single event.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Appearance and evidence: らしい
grammar.explanation:
らしい can express an inference from external information or typical qualities of a category. Distinguish 'apparently a student' from 'student-like' in context.

Formation: Evidence-based らしい follows a plain predicate; nouns normally attach directly. Noun + らしい can also mean typical of that noun.

Usage and cautions: Context distinguishes information-based “apparently” from characteristic “-like”. 学生らしい may therefore need surrounding evidence. Nouns do not take だ before evidential らしい. Unlike そうだ hearsay, らしい often presents the speaker’s inference from indirect information.

examples.ja: 駅前に新しい店ができたらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently a new shop has opened near the station.

examples.ja: 天気予報では、明日は晴れるらしいです。
examples.reading: てんきよほうでは、あしたははれるらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently tomorrow will be sunny, according to the forecast.

examples.ja: 今日は春らしい暖かさです。
examples.reading: きょうははるらしいあたたかさです。
examples.en: Today has a warmth typical of spring.

questions.prompt: Choose the likely evidential reading of 雨が降るらしい.
choices: I intend to make it rain
I can hear the rain directly
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “Apparently it will rain”. らしい reports an inference or information rather than an intention.

questions.prompt: Use an evidential noun predicate: あの人は医者＿。
questions.explanation: Nouns normally attach directly to らしい: 医者らしい can mean apparently a doctor, depending on context.

questions.prompt: In 子供らしい笑顔, what does らしい convey?
choices: A smile characteristic of a child
A rumor that someone smiled yesterday
questions.explanation: Here らしい modifies 笑顔 through the category 子供, describing a characteristically childlike smile.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 天気予報では、明日は晴れるらしいです。
choices: Tomorrow is guaranteed to be rainy.
I want to make tomorrow sunny.
Yesterday looked sunny from the window.
Apparently tomorrow will be sunny, according to the forecast.
questions.explanation: “天気予報では、明日は晴れるらしいです。” means “Apparently tomorrow will be sunny, according to the forecast.” in this example. Context distinguishes information-based “apparently” from characteristic “-like”.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 今日は春らしい暖かさです。
choices: Today is colder than any winter day.
It is apparently not warm today.
Today has a warmth typical of spring.
I heard that spring has been canceled.
questions.explanation: “今日は春らしい暖かさです。” means “Today has a warmth typical of spring.” in this example. Context distinguishes information-based “apparently” from characteristic “-like”.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Inference: ようだ・みたいだ
grammar.explanation:
ようだ expresses a judgment from evidence; みたいだ is a conversational counterpart. Nouns use のようだ but usually attach directly to みたいだ.

Formation: Verb / い-adjective + ようだ; noun + のようだ; な-adjective + なようだ. Conversational みたいだ attaches directly to nouns.

Usage and cautions: These forms can express an inference from evidence or a resemblance. みたい is conversational and not the past of 見る. Use ような / みたいな before nouns and ように / みたいに before actions. Explain the evidence when an inference might otherwise sound unsupported.

examples.ja: 外は静かで、雪が降っているようです。
examples.en: It is quiet outside; it seems to be snowing.

examples.ja: 足音がします。誰か来たようです。
examples.reading: あしおとがします。だれかきたようです。
examples.en: I hear footsteps. It seems someone has arrived.

examples.ja: この雲は魚みたいです。
examples.reading: このくもはさかなみたいです。
examples.en: This cloud looks like a fish.

questions.prompt: Complete a noun comparison: 夢＿だ。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “のよう”. A noun links to よう with の: 夢のようだ.

questions.prompt: Complete a な-adjective inference: 部屋は静か＿ようです。
questions.explanation: A な-adjective takes な before よう: 静かなようです; a noun instead takes の.

questions.prompt: Choose a conversational noun resemblance.
choices: あの岩は顔のみたいだ。
あの岩は顔だみたいだ。
あの岩は顔なみたいだ。
questions.explanation: A noun directly precedes みたい: 顔みたいだ; の is needed with 顔のようだ, not with みたい.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 足音がします。誰か来たようです。
choices: Please come here without making a sound.
Someone told me not to listen for footsteps.
I hear footsteps. It seems someone has arrived.
I hear footsteps, so nobody can have arrived.
questions.explanation: “足音がします。誰か来たようです。” means “I hear footsteps. It seems someone has arrived.” in this example. These forms can express an inference from evidence or a resemblance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この雲は魚みたいです。
choices: The fish has eaten the cloud.
This cloud looks like a fish.
This fish looks like a cloudless sky.
I want to see fish in a cloud.
questions.explanation: “この雲は魚みたいです。” means “This cloud looks like a fish.” in this example. These forms can express an inference from evidence or a resemblance.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Despite: のに
grammar.explanation:
Clause + のに expresses a result contrary to expectation, often with surprise or dissatisfaction. Nouns and な-adjectives take なのに.

Formation: Verb / い-adjective + のに; noun / な-adjective + なのに. A past noun predicate uses だったのに.

Usage and cautions: The second clause contradicts an expectation raised by the first, often with surprise or dissatisfaction. This is not a neutral reason. Do not use it as the ordinary connector for a purposeful request. Separate this concessive のに from purpose のに in 読むのに便利.

examples.ja: たくさん寝たのに、まだ眠いです。
examples.en: Although I slept a lot, I am still sleepy.

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだのに、まだ頭が痛いです。
examples.reading: くすりをのんだのに、まだあたまがいたいです。
examples.en: Although I took medicine, my head still hurts.

examples.ja: この部屋は静かなのに、よく眠れません。
examples.reading: このへやはしずかなのに、よくねむれません。
examples.en: Although this room is quiet, I cannot sleep well.

questions.prompt: Complete: 休日＿、仕事があります。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “なのに”. A noun such as 休日 takes なのに, not だのに.

questions.prompt: Complete a contradictory adjective result: 安い＿、誰も買いません。
questions.explanation: 安いのに contrasts low price with the unexpected lack of buyers.

questions.prompt: Connect a past noun predicate: 昨日は休み＿、働きました。
questions.explanation: The past noun predicate is 休みだった; append のに to form 休みだったのに.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 薬を飲んだのに、まだ頭が痛いです。
choices: My headache stopped before I took medicine.
Although I took medicine, my head still hurts.
My head hurts because I refused to take medicine.
I will take medicine so that my head hurts.
questions.explanation: “薬を飲んだのに、まだ頭が痛いです。” means “Although I took medicine, my head still hurts.” in this example. The second clause contradicts an expectation raised by the first, often with surprise or dissatisfaction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この部屋は静かなのに、よく眠れません。
choices: Although this room is quiet, I cannot sleep well.
I sleep well because the room is quiet.
The room becomes quiet whenever I sleep.
Please keep the room quiet while I sleep.
questions.explanation: “この部屋は静かなのに、よく眠れません。” means “Although this room is quiet, I cannot sleep well.” in this example. The second clause contradicts an expectation raised by the first, often with surprise or dissatisfaction.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Causes: おかげで・せいで
grammar.explanation:
おかげで credits a usually positive outcome; せいで attributes a usually negative one. Both may follow a clause or noun + の.

Formation: Plain clause + おかげで / せいで; noun + の; な-adjective + な before either expression.

Usage and cautions: おかげで normally credits a helpful cause, while せいで attributes blame for an unfavorable outcome. Irony can reverse the usual emotional reading, so context matters. Neutral ために may be better when you do not want to express thanks or blame.

examples.ja: 先生のおかげで、試験に合格しました。
examples.en: Thanks to my teacher, I passed the exam.

examples.ja: 友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、早く終わりました。
examples.reading: ともだちがてつだってくれたおかげで、はやくおわりました。
examples.en: Thanks to my friend’s help, I finished early.

examples.ja: 寝不足のせいで、授業に集中できません。
examples.reading: ねぶそくのせいで、じゅぎょうにしゅうちゅうできません。
examples.en: Because of lack of sleep, I cannot concentrate in class.

questions.prompt: Choose a positive attribution: 友達の＿助かりました。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “おかげで”. おかげで normally credits beneficial help.

questions.prompt: Credit a helpful noun cause: 皆さん＿おかげで成功しました。
questions.explanation: A noun takes の before おかげで: 皆さんのおかげで credits everyone’s help.

questions.prompt: Blame traffic for a late arrival: 渋滞の＿遅れました。
questions.explanation: せいで assigns an unfavorable outcome to the traffic jam; it explicitly carries blame here.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、早く終わりました。
choices: Thanks to my friend’s help, I finished early.
My friend’s help prevented me from finishing.
I finished before my friend began helping.
I was forced to help my friend finish late.
questions.explanation: “友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、早く終わりました。” means “Thanks to my friend’s help, I finished early.” in this example. おかげで normally credits a helpful cause, while せいで attributes blame for an unfavorable outcome.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 寝不足のせいで、授業に集中できません。
choices: Thanks to enough sleep, I can concentrate well.
I cannot sleep because I enjoy class.
The class helps me sleep deeply.
Because of lack of sleep, I cannot concentrate in class.
questions.explanation: “寝不足のせいで、授業に集中できません。” means “Because of lack of sleep, I cannot concentrate in class.” in this example. おかげで normally credits a helpful cause, while せいで attributes blame for an unfavorable outcome.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: While a state lasts: うちに
grammar.explanation:
うちに means while a state remains or before it changes. It can also describe an unintended change occurring during an ongoing activity.

Formation: Verb dictionary / ている / negative + うちに; い-adjective + うちに; な-adjective + な; noun + の.

Usage and cautions: Act while a favorable state lasts, before it changes. With an ongoing action, an unplanned change can happen during it. Negative ないうちに often means before doing or before something happens. Do not treat うちに as an exact clock interval.

examples.ja: 温かいうちに食べてください。
examples.en: Please eat it while it is warm.

examples.ja: 明るいうちに帰りましょう。
examples.reading: あかるいうちにかえりましょう。
examples.en: Let’s go home while it is still light.

examples.ja: 本を読んでいるうちに、眠くなりました。
examples.reading: ほんをよんでいるうちに、ねむくなりました。
examples.en: While reading a book, I became sleepy.

questions.prompt: Choose 'before you forget'.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “忘れないうちに”. ないうちに means before the negative state ceases: before forgetting.

questions.prompt: Say “while still a student”: 学生＿うちに旅行したいです。
questions.explanation: A noun links with の: 学生のうちに means during the time when one is still a student.

questions.prompt: Choose “before the rain starts”.
choices: 雨が降ってからでないと
questions.explanation: 降らないうちに refers to the period while it is not yet raining, hence before the rain starts.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 明るいうちに帰りましょう。
choices: Let’s stay until it is completely dark.
We went home only because the lights broke.
It became light after we went home.
Let’s go home while it is still light.
questions.explanation: “明るいうちに帰りましょう。” means “Let’s go home while it is still light.” in this example. Act while a favorable state lasts, before it changes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 本を読んでいるうちに、眠くなりました。
choices: I decided to read in order to become sleepy.
I was too sleepy to start reading.
While reading a book, I became sleepy.
I read a book only after waking up.
questions.explanation: “本を読んでいるうちに、眠くなりました。” means “While reading a book, I became sleepy.” in this example. Act while a favorable state lasts, before it changes.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Throughout a period: 間・間に
grammar.explanation:
間 emphasizes a state or activity continuing over an interval. 間に locates an event or change somewhere within that interval.

Formation: Verb ている / dictionary form + 間（に）; noun + の間（に）; な-adjective + な間（に）.

Usage and cautions: 間 describes a state or action over the interval; 間に locates an occurrence or change within it. The difference is not simply long versus short. Ask whether the main predicate continues throughout or happens at some point within the period.

examples.ja: 留守の間に、荷物が届きました。
examples.en: A parcel arrived while I was out.

examples.ja: 子供が寝ている間、静かにしていました。
examples.reading: こどもがねているあいだ、しずかにしていました。
examples.en: I stayed quiet while the child was sleeping.

examples.ja: 買い物をしている間に、雨がやみました。
examples.reading: かいものをしているあいだに、あめがやみました。
examples.en: The rain stopped while I was shopping.

questions.prompt: A one-time arrival during absence uses which?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “留守の間に”. 間に places a bounded event inside a larger time interval.

questions.prompt: A state continues throughout the trip: 旅行の＿、ずっと元気でした。
questions.explanation: 間 with ずっと元気 describes health throughout the trip; 間に一度 would mark one occurrence.

questions.prompt: A single phone call occurred during a bath: お風呂に入っている＿、電話がありました。
questions.explanation: 間に places the call at some point within the bathing interval, rather than describing a continuing activity throughout it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 子供が寝ている間、静かにしていました。
choices: The child slept because I left the room.
I fell asleep before the child.
I stayed quiet while the child was sleeping.
I made noise after the child woke up.
questions.explanation: “子供が寝ている間、静かにしていました。” means “I stayed quiet while the child was sleeping.” in this example. 間 describes a state or action over the interval; 間に locates an occurrence or change within it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 買い物をしている間に、雨がやみました。
choices: I could not shop because the rain never stopped.
The rain stopped while I was shopping.
It rained continuously only after I finished shopping.
I went shopping in order to stop the rain.
questions.explanation: “買い物をしている間に、雨がやみました。” means “The rain stopped while I was shopping.” in this example. 間 describes a state or action over the interval; 間に locates an occurrence or change within it.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: On each occasion: たびに
grammar.explanation:
Dictionary form or noun + の followed by たびに means every time. It links repeated occasions with a recurring consequence.

Formation: Dictionary verb + たびに; noun + のたびに. A repeated occasion regularly triggers the main result.

Usage and cautions: Use this for recurring occasions, often with a fresh reaction each time. It is not a marker for one isolated future appointment. Keep the verb in dictionary form. A routine controlled action may sound more natural with と or 毎回 depending on context.

examples.ja: この曲を聞くたびに、故郷を思い出します。
examples.en: Every time I hear this song, I remember my hometown.

examples.ja: この写真を見るたびに、旅行を思い出します。
examples.reading: このしゃしんをみるたびに、りょこうをおもいだします。
examples.en: Every time I see this photo, I remember the trip.

examples.ja: 試験のたびに、緊張します。
examples.reading: しけんのたびに、きんちょうします。
examples.en: I get nervous every time there is an exam.

questions.prompt: Complete: 会う＿、元気をもらう。
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “たびに”. たびに marks each repeated meeting as an occasion.

questions.prompt: Complete a recurring meeting effect: 彼に会う＿、新しい話を聞きます。
questions.explanation: 会うたびに means on every meeting occasion; the sentence links repeated meetings with hearing something new.

questions.prompt: Use the noun connection: 出張＿たびに、お土産を買います。
questions.explanation: A noun such as 出張 requires の before たびに; dictionary verbs attach directly.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この写真を見るたびに、旅行を思い出します。
choices: I never remember the trip when I see this photo.
Every time I see this photo, I remember the trip.
I took this photo after forgetting the trip.
I see the photo only when I travel abroad.
questions.explanation: “この写真を見るたびに、旅行を思い出します。” means “Every time I see this photo, I remember the trip.” in this example. Use this for recurring occasions, often with a fresh reaction each time.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 試験のたびに、緊張します。
choices: I get nervous every time there is an exam.
I was nervous only once after an exam.
I take an exam whenever I feel relaxed.
I have never felt nervous about exams.
questions.explanation: “試験のたびに、緊張します。” means “I get nervous every time there is an exam.” in this example. Use this for recurring occasions, often with a fresh reaction each time.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Passive voice
grammar.explanation:
Godan verbs use the a-row + れる; ichidan verbs use stem + られる. Passive sentences focus on the affected party and can imply an unwelcome effect.

Formation: Godan a-row + れる: 読まれる; ichidan stem + られる: 食べられる; する→される; 来る→来られる.

Usage and cautions: The affected party becomes the topic or subject, and the actor often takes に. Indirect passive can express inconvenience, but direct passive need not be negative. Some ichidan passive forms look identical to potential forms; context and particles distinguish them.

examples.ja: 私は先生に褒められました。
examples.en: I was praised by my teacher.

examples.ja: 私は友達に写真を撮られました。
examples.reading: わたしはともだちにしゃしんをとられました。
examples.en: My friend took a photo of me.

examples.ja: この橋は百年前に建てられました。
examples.reading: このはしはひゃくねんまえにたてられました。
examples.en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.

questions.prompt: Choose the passive of 書く.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “書かれる”. 書かれる is passive; 書ける potential and 書かせる causative.

questions.prompt: Choose the passive of 盗む.
questions.explanation: 盗む is godan: the a-row stem 盗ま combines with れる; 盗める is potential and 盗ませる causative.

questions.prompt: Mark the actor in a passive: 私は先生＿褒められました。
questions.explanation: In this direct passive, 先生に identifies the person who praised the speaker; 私 is the praised party.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 私は友達に写真を撮られました。
choices: My friend took a photo of me.
I took a photo of my friend.
My friend let me take a photo.
I wanted to take my friend’s photo.
questions.explanation: “私は友達に写真を撮られました。” means “My friend took a photo of me.” in this example. The affected party becomes the topic or subject, and the actor often takes に.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この橋は百年前に建てられました。
choices: This bridge will be built in a hundred years.
The bridge built a house a hundred years ago.
This bridge must not be built.
This bridge was built a hundred years ago.
questions.explanation: “この橋は百年前に建てられました。” means “This bridge was built a hundred years ago.” in this example. The affected party becomes the topic or subject, and the actor often takes に.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Causative voice
grammar.explanation:
Godan a-row + せる and ichidan stem + させる express making or allowing someone to act. The forceful or permissive reading depends on context.

Formation: Godan a-row + せる: 書かせる; ichidan stem + させる: 食べさせる; する→させる; 来る→来させる.

Usage and cautions: A causative can mean make or let, depending on authority and willingness. The person acting takes を or に according to the verb and construction. With a transitive verb, use に for the actor when the object already takes を: 子供に野菜を食べさせる.

examples.ja: 母は子供を遊ばせました。
examples.en: The mother let her child play.

examples.ja: 先生は学生に作文を書かせました。
examples.reading: せんせいはがくせいにさくぶんをかかせました。
examples.en: The teacher had the students write an essay.

examples.ja: 父は私を一人で旅行させてくれました。
examples.reading: ちちはわたしをひとりでりょこうさせてくれました。
examples.en: My father kindly let me travel alone.

questions.prompt: Choose the causative of 食べる.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “食べさせる”. 食べさせる means make or let someone eat.

questions.prompt: Choose the causative of 読む.
questions.explanation: 読む is godan; 読ま + せる yields 読ませる, meaning make or let someone read.

questions.prompt: Choose the actor particle: 母は弟＿野菜を食べさせました。
questions.explanation: 野菜を is the direct object, so 弟に marks the person made or allowed to eat; avoid two ordinary を objects.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 先生は学生に作文を書かせました。
choices: The students had the teacher write an essay.
The teacher was praised for an essay.
The students were unable to write an essay.
The teacher had the students write an essay.
questions.explanation: “先生は学生に作文を書かせました。” means “The teacher had the students write an essay.” in this example. A causative can mean make or let, depending on authority and willingness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 父は私を一人で旅行させてくれました。
choices: I let my father travel alone.
My father traveled alone instead of me.
My father kindly let me travel alone.
My father forced me to stay home alone.
questions.explanation: “父は私を一人で旅行させてくれました。” means “My father kindly let me travel alone.” in this example. A causative can mean make or let, depending on authority and willingness.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Respectful and humble language
grammar.explanation:
Respectful forms raise the other person's actions; humble forms lower one's own side in relation to others. They are not interchangeable polite synonyms.

Formation: Respectful forms describe the respected person: いらっしゃる, 召し上がる, なさる. Humble forms describe one’s own side: 伺う, いただく, いたす.

Usage and cautions: Choose a form by whose action it is, not simply by the presence of a senior person. In outside-company speech your company belongs to your own side. です / ます supplies politeness but does not by itself determine honorific direction. Avoid raising yourself with a respectful verb.

examples.ja: 先生はもういらっしゃいました。
examples.en: The teacher has already arrived.

examples.ja: 先生は何を召し上がりますか。
examples.reading: せんせいはなにをめしあがりますか。
examples.en: What will the teacher eat or drink?

examples.ja: 明日、御社に伺います。
examples.reading: あした、おんしゃにうかがいます。
examples.en: I will visit your company tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Which humbly describes your own visit?
choices: 召し上がりますでしょう
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “伺います”. 伺う is humble 'visit/ask'; いらっしゃる and 召し上がる honor others.

questions.prompt: Respectfully ask about the teacher’s presence: 先生は研究室に＿か。
questions.explanation: いらっしゃる respectfully describes another person’s being or going; おる and 参る are humble, and 申す means say.

questions.prompt: Humbly describe your own action: 私が資料を説明＿。
questions.explanation: いたす is humble する, so 説明いたします lowers the speaker’s action appropriately.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 先生は何を召し上がりますか。
choices: Please make the teacher cook something.
The teacher asked me what I ate yesterday.
What will the teacher eat or drink?
What will I humbly eat for the teacher?
questions.explanation: “先生は何を召し上がりますか。” means “What will the teacher eat or drink?” in this example. Choose a form by whose action it is, not simply by the presence of a senior person.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 明日、御社に伺います。
choices: Please do not visit our company tomorrow.
I will visit your company tomorrow.
Your company will visit me tomorrow.
questions.explanation: “明日、御社に伺います。” means “I will visit your company tomorrow.” in this example. Choose a form by whose action it is, not simply by the presence of a senior person.
